prompt.context: Your client is a global consumer packaged goods company — Grime Co. Grime Co. makes paper products (like paper towels), home cleaning products, and laundry care products. The company's Board of Directors has set an aggressive revenue target of $2 billion four years from now. Currently, revenues are $1 billion. The CEO has come to you to ask for help.
prompt.question: Evaluate the company's position and help develop a strategy to deliver top-line net sales of $2 billion by 2025. (Net sales = retail sales minus trade spend, where trade spend is what manufacturers pay distributors or retailers to incentivize them to sell products to end consumers.)

clarifying_info.q: How are current revenues split across the three product categories?
clarifying_info.a: Sales are divided evenly between the three categories — approximately 33% each.

clarifying_info.q: What is the market growth rate?
clarifying_info.a: The overall market is growing at 10% per year, and Grime Co. expects to maintain a constant market share. At 10% compounded over four years, market growth alone would bring sales to approximately $1.5 billion by 2025.

clarifying_info.q: Is growth the same across all three categories?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, growth is about the same across all three categories.

clarifying_info.q: What organic growth strategies has the client considered?
clarifying_info.a: The client has a new toilet cleaning product in development that analysts believe will do well. It is near launch, priced at $5 per unit, requires 20% trade spend per product to reach its volume target, and is expected to sell 40 million units on average per year. No additional investment is required beyond what has already been spent (sunk cost). Other organic strategies such as price adjustments, advertising increases, vertical integration, and promotions are not viable at this time.
The Corporate Development department has identified two high-priority acquisition targets: Organoclean and Home Defense Inc. The client can only purchase one of them.

clarifying_info.q: Does Grime Co. have any stated values or constraints?
clarifying_info.a: The company has a strong stance in favor of sustainability.

framework: Market growth: assess how much revenue growth comes from maintaining market share in a growing market
Organic growth: identify internal actions to drive additional revenue — focus on new products (price adjustments, advertising, vertical integration, promotions are not viable)
Inorganic growth: evaluate acquisition or joint venture targets to close the remaining gap
Synergy analysis: assess positive and negative synergies for each acquisition target before recommending one

questions.prompt: How much revenue will Grime Co. generate by 2025 from market growth alone, and how large is the remaining gap to the $2B target?
questions.guidance: Market grows at 10% compounded over 4 years on a $1B base, yielding roughly $1.5B. Gap = $2B - $1.5B = $500M deficit remaining.

questions.prompt: How much incremental net sales does the new toilet cleaning product contribute annually by 2025?
questions.guidance: Candidate must apply trade spend to get net sales per unit, then multiply by expected volume. Revenue = $5/unit × (1 - 20%) × 40M units = $4/unit × 40M = $160M. New deficit after this product = $500M - $160M = $340M.

math.setup: Net price per unit = $5 × (1 - 0.20) = $4; Annual net sales = $4 × 40M units

questions.prompt: Project 2025 net sales for both acquisition targets and identify which one, on sales alone, closes more of the $340M gap.
questions.guidance: Organoclean: $150M growing at 10%/yr for 4 years ≈ $220M (round to nearest $10M). Home Defense Inc.: $200M growing at 20%/yr for 4 years ≈ $410M (round to nearest $10M). On raw 2025 sales, Home Defense appears to close more of the gap.

questions.prompt: What positive and negative synergies should Grime Co. consider when evaluating Organoclean vs. Home Defense Inc.?
questions.guidance: Candidate should brainstorm multiple synergy types. Key ones to surface: (1) Positive — Grime Co. can leverage its Europe distribution network to generate additional sales of $40M in year 1, expected to triple in 4 years (~$120M), applicable to both targets. (2) Negative — Grime Co. will not sell harmful chemicals; all of Home Defense's bug killers fall into this category and cannot be reformulated or sold, so those products must be discontinued. Bug killers = 25% of Home Defense sales. At 2025 sales of $410M, 25% = ~$102.5M lost. Other synergies to consider: procurement, manufacturing, back-office, co-branding, scale (positive); corporate culture mismatch, antitrust, mission/values clash, brand dilution (negative).

math.setup: Home Defense lost sales: 25% × $410M; Europe distribution synergy: $40M yr1 tripling over 4 years ≈ $120M in yr4
steps: Home Defense net: $500M - $160M (product) - $410M (Home Defense 2025) + $102.5M (lost bug killer sales) = $32.5M deficit
math.answer: Organoclean closes the gap exactly ($0 deficit); Home Defense still leaves a $32.5M deficit after accounting for discontinued bug killer products

brainstorming.prompt: What are the positive and negative synergies Grime Co. should consider when evaluating an acquisition target?

categories.name: Positive synergies
ideas: Distribution synergies (e.g., leverage Europe distribution network for additional sales)
Procurement synergies (shared purchasing power reduces COGS)
Manufacturing synergies (shared facilities or production lines)
Back-office synergies (shared finance, HR, IT infrastructure)
Co-branding new products across combined portfolio
Scale synergies (larger combined entity achieves better economics)

categories.name: Negative synergies
ideas: Mission or values clash (e.g., sustainability stance conflicts with target's products)
Brand dilution from association with incompatible product lines
Forced product discontinuation when target products cannot be sold under acquirer's values (e.g., harmful chemicals in bug killers)

recommendation: Although market growth and the launch of a new toilet cleaning product get Grime Co. to approximately $1.66 billion in net sales by 2025, the $2 billion target will not be met through organic means alone.

Therefore, Grime Co. should also pursue growth through acquisition. Of the two targets, we recommend purchasing Organoclean. Its 2025 projected sales of $220M plus $120M in Europe distribution synergies, combined with the new product contribution of $160M and $500M in market growth, allows Grime Co. to reach exactly the $2B net sales target by 2025. Home Defense Inc., despite higher raw sales, leaves a $32.5M deficit after required discontinuation of harmful bug killer products (25% of its sales), which conflicts with Grime Co.'s sustainability values.
risks: Growth trajectory of acquisition target could change, making projections unreliable
Purchase price for the target could be too high to afford or destroy value
Target could be unprofitable — case focuses on top-line sales only
Doubling in size over four years could itself be a risk — integration challenges from rapid scaling
next_steps: Verify assumptions (synergy estimates, growth projections) and assign internal roles
Establish contact with the target to gauge acquisition interest and terms
Conduct detailed valuation and determine BATNA
Roll out new toilet cleaning product per existing launch plan
